findings.evidence: features/005-scope-change-skill/005-scope-change-skill-prd.md:AC-8 + R8 — AC-8 verifies that the impact-list file's source sections list 'every entry where `feature == {NNN-slug}` AND `status` ∈ {`planned`, `in_progress`, `review`} AND the entry's Anchor R-ID is in the changed-R-ID set' for `task-history.json`, similarly for Linear (`In Progress`, `In Review`), and PR/test-plan sections. The boundary 'in-flight' is partially defined per source — but the ACROSS-SOURCE definition of 'in-flight' has a non-binary gap: an open PR with `--draft` flag is `state == open` per `gh pr list --state open` (so it surfaces) but is conventionally not 'in-flight' in the reviewer-ready sense; a Linear ticket whose status is a project-defined custom 'Blocked' or 'On Hold' state is neither in `In Progress` nor `In Review` but is also not closed. AC-8 doesn't tell a fresh agent unambiguously whether to include or exclude these. The lens question fails: 'Could a fresh agent run the impact-list compilation in isolation and report pass/fail unambiguously on whether the list is complete?' — answer: depends on whether the agent's interpretation of 'in-flight' includes draft PRs and Linear blocked-state tickets.
findings.claim: Non-binary acceptance criterion at the across-source boundary — AC-8 enumerates the in-flight statuses for `task-history.json` and Linear cleanly, but the open-PR clause uses `gh pr list --state open` without naming whether `--draft` PRs are in-scope, and the Linear clause hard-codes only the canonical `In Progress` / `In Review` statuses without naming what to do with project-defined custom intermediate states (Blocked, On Hold, In Review — Stakeholder, etc.). A fresh agent reviewing the impact list cannot tell whether a draft PR's omission is a bug or correct behaviour; the AC fails the Goal-Driven Execution binary-test lens.
findings.proposed_change: Sharpen AC-8 (and R8 by reference) to name the boundary explicitly. Concrete edit: 'AC-8 additionally specifies — (a) Open PRs: `gh pr list --state open` includes draft PRs by default; v1 INCLUDES draft PRs in the impact list (a draft PR with overlapping touched files is in-flight work in the rebase-or-close sense); the impact-list entry annotates `(draft)` for draft PRs so the user can triage accordingly. (b) Linear: only the literal canonical statuses `In Progress` and `In Review` count by default; project-defined custom intermediate statuses (Blocked, On Hold, etc.) are NOT auto-included — a chat-line note at impact-list compilation surfaces `(Linear: N tickets in custom statuses {list} not auto-included; review manually if relevant)` so the user knows the boundary was applied. The hard-coded canonical-statuses-only rule keeps the AC binary; surfacing the count-of-skipped via chat-line keeps the user informed.' Update R8 to reference the boundary explicitly, not implicitly via Linear status enumeration.

findings.evidence: features/005-scope-change-skill/005-scope-change-skill-prd.md:AC-13 + R12 — AC-13 verifies parent-context token consumption stays under 25K and per-sub-skill-invocation growth stays under 2K, citing `specflow:budget --skill specflow:scope-change` as the verification tool. R12 establishes orchestrator-pattern compliance as the requirement. The reverse trace check: AC-13 verifies a token-budget contract; R12 promises orchestrator-pattern compliance with per-sub-skill 'intermediate artefacts land in `admin/scratch/...` and only file paths return to the parent context'. R12 says nothing about token-budget caps — the 25K/2K numbers in AC-13 are introduced in the AC without any R-level requirement establishing them. The architectural anchor (orchestrator-pattern.md target) is real, but the R-level expression in this PRD body does not name the numeric bounds. Orphan AC: AC-13 verifies a contract (specific token bounds) that no R-level requirement establishes.
findings.claim: Orphan AC (E4 reverse traceability) — AC-13 verifies token-budget bounds (25K parent-context, 2K per-sub-skill) that no R-level requirement in the Requirements section actually mandates. R12 promises orchestrator-pattern compliance but is silent on the numeric bounds; the bounds are introduced in AC-13 without a stated R. Goal-Driven Execution reverse-trace rule: every AC must trace to ≥1 R, just as every R must be covered by ≥1 AC. AC-13's claim cites the orchestrator-pattern target but the Phase 1 architectural rule has no R-level expression in this PRD body for the specific 25K/2K numbers (which are tighter than `specflow:develop`'s 30K cap and therefore a scope-change-specific calibration that needs naming).
findings.proposed_change: Add a new requirement R13 that explicitly establishes the token-budget bounds: 'R13. Token-budget bounds. Parent-context token consumption across the eight-step flow stays under 25K tokens (tighter than `specflow:develop`'s 30K because scope-change has fewer sub-skill steps and the impact-list compilation in step (vi) is the only parent-context aggregation). Per-sub-skill-invocation growth stays under 2K tokens (verbatim file content is read via command substitution into the sub-skill fork; only file paths and the closing-decision summary return to the parent). Trace: codebase context (pre-grilling) — Sister Phase 1 orchestrators bullet (orchestrator-pattern.md target). Serves goal: Outcome (artefacts co-located; downstream skills read the full chain).' Then update AC-13's `Verifies:` line from `R12` to `R13` (or `R12 + R13` if both are intended). This closes the orphan-AC gap and makes the Phase 1 architectural calibration scope-change-specific at the R-level.
